subject: O Level E-Math
title: Tangents to a circle
question:
The points A, B, C, D and E lie on a circle with centre O. The lines HI and BI are tangents to the circle at C and B respectively. BC intersects AE at G. Given that ∠ABC = 76°, ∠OAB = 62° and ∠DAE = 70°.
(i) Show that triangle OBI is congruent to triangle OCI.
(ii) Find angle DCB, angle GCO and angle BCH.
referenceNote: The original figure from the exam paper. It is not drawn to scale.

scene: Claude worked out where each point sits from the angles in the question, and the renderer placed the tangents and intersections exactly.
Drawn to scale, point I ends up far from the circle. The original figure pulls it closer so it fits on the page.

Correct on the first try, but changing any angle means redoing about twenty numbers.
